The system operates under a fail-closed principle, rejecting any deviation from this schema without attempting repair. The validator performs three core checks: shape conformance (47 signals), verdict completeness (all 6 dimensions present), and JSON validity. These checks map to a Boolean lattice where each node represents a signal's verdict tuple. The system's integrity is maintained by ensuring that no modification occurs to the registry, preserving its provenance. Git-based drift detection adds temporal context, identifying when the registry diverges from HEAD. This architecture enforces a strict separation between data ingestion and validation, aligning with the principle that registry generation is not automated but relies on manual or external processes.
